I've opened https://github.com/thefundamentaltheor3m/Sphere-Packing-Lean/issues/346 to capture the work involved in moving over to the module system.

I aim to have a PR for that later today.
PR moving the codebase onto the module system: https://github.com/thefundamentaltheor3m/Sphere-Packing-Lean/pull/347
I'm not sure who's best to review this. I basically followed the pattern used in cslib and mathlib (eg. here).
I'm repurposing this topic into one focused on keeping Gauss's PR rebased against the latest main. This will be a long-running task, so we might as well have a channel for it.

Upon discussion with @Auguste Poiroux, I've squashed the 18 commits in the Gauss PR into 1 commit, which is temporarily living at the branch asr/gauss-rebase(here). The rebase is mostly mechanical, but every now and then there's a change that I'm unsure what to do with. My plan is to ask for advice here, adding temporary TODOs as placeholders until we reach consensus on what to do.

1) Gauss contributed the following lemma 

lemma D_isZeroAtImInfty_of_bounded {f : ℍ → ℂ}
    (hf : MDifferentiable 𝓘(ℂ) 𝓘(ℂ) f)
    (hbdd : IsBoundedAtImInfty f) :
    IsZeroAtImInfty (D f)

while @Cameron Freer has the similar:

theorem D_tendsto_zero_of_isBoundedAtImInfty {f : ℍ → ℂ}
    (hf : MDifferentiable 𝓘(ℂ) 𝓘(ℂ) f)
    (hbdd : IsBoundedAtImInfty f) :
    Filter.Tendsto (D f) atImInfty (nhds 0)

Question: Are we going to be refactoring most of Gauss's proof to use the Tendsto? Are we comfortable leaving both lemmas in for now, with a TODO saying we'll probably remove Gauss's version later?
We should be using IsZeroAtImInfty I think, since thats what the modular form API is built around. If needed then we could make some more API to make things easier to prove.
@Chris Birkbeck thanks, makes sense. Do you have any thoughts on how this might interact with the tendsto_cont tactic (spherepacking#330)? Is there another version of this that might be more useful?
Also, a small note is that as of last week, we can just write hf as hf : MDiff f since it should be able to infer the manifold with corners structure.
I think we can replace all MDifferentiable to MDiff, probably do this in a single PR - I can do this today real quick

so this is defined as some tendsto, but I guess we the tactic cant open the definition to see this? Could we flag this definition as a tendsto_cont defn that could then be done with the tactic? like we do with like fun_prop etc?

Or we could maybe make ZeroAtFilter, etc, an abbrev and then the tactic might work? I think originally these definitions were made back in the lean 3 days, when I don't even know if we could abbrev things (certainly I didn't know about it back then).

Chris Birkbeck 말함:

Also, a small note is that as of last week, we can just write hf as hf : MDiff f since it should be able to infer the manifold with corners structure.

PR#355
I'll take a look at merging in the lean-v4.28.0 bump, if nobody else is looking at it

The version bump, removed the lemma prod_tendstoUniformlyOn_tprod' from eta.lean. However, the Gauss branch uses that lemma here.

@Seewoo Lee is there an upstream version of this lemma that we should now be using?
We can probably use docs#Summable.hasProdUniformlyOn_nat_one_add which is now in mathlib.

I guess that's what codex implicitly did in bump PR too, change can be found in Eisenstein.lean https://github.com/thefundamentaltheor3m/Sphere-Packing-Lean/pull/332/changes#diff-3e4389cb90a7903de6cb37462e892065ff126bf8459c434e290da09c7fbac04eR694

I'm noticing that Gauss commented out a bunch of lemmas in RamanujanIdenties.lean: https://github.com/thefundamentaltheor3m/Sphere-Packing-Lean/blob/149b423a08b2b2a9bbaf4874060bc270035ba1cf/SpherePacking/ModularForms/RamanujanIdentities.lean#L54-L152
also in DimensionFormulas.lean: https://github.com/thefundamentaltheor3m/Sphere-Packing-Lean/blob/149b423a08b2b2a9bbaf4874060bc270035ba1cf/SpherePacking/ModularForms/DimensionFormulas.lean#L47-L100
oh those we do need for the dimension formulas
Sorry, I missed the recent discussion here.

spherepacking#356 is a reopening of the big Gauss PR (spherepacking#341), rebased onto the latest main. In particular, this rebases on top of the changes to bump to Lean 4.28.0, and the migration onto the module system.

This was a pretty painful rebase, but I'm optimistic that as we land future changes, it'll be relatively simple to rebase this on top of them. In particular, if we simply extract changes from this PR, improve them, and land them in main, it'll be pretty straigtforward to rebase this branch onto that (mutatis mutandis).

I had to open this as a new PR from a new branch called gauss2 because I didn't want to force push to the existing gauss branch and clobber @Auguste Poiroux's work. We can close this PR and integrate the changes differently if people prefer!

I had some in-progress work on that rebase. I'll open pull requests to the gauss2 branch where I notice things that @Aayush Rajasekaran missed. Here is a first one: https://github.com/thefundamentaltheor3m/Sphere-Packing-Lean/pull/357
Perfect, thank you! When in doubt, I opted to keep more rather than delete, so there's likely a few other easy ways to reduce the diff like this.
feel free to squash my diffs into the one big commit, if that is the most convenient thing

Yeah, we should discuss how we want to keep this PR going. I think maintaining it at one commit would be nice for future rebasing, but we can still land changes one commit at a time.

Perhaps we just say every Friday evening, we squash everything in it into one commit, and rebase onto latest main?
What are the downsides of not continually keeping it squashed and up-to-date? I suppose that could be annoying new PRs that are based on it?

By the way, I really like that we now have a progress bar. We want to make these numbers smaller and smaller:
image.png

David Renshaw said:

What are the downsides of not continually keeping it squashed and up-to-date? I suppose that could be annoying new PRs that are based on it?

Yeah, I think we should do that -- it's just a matter of whether "continually" is "once a week" / "once a day" / "every time a commit lands". I think any of them would work, I'm not too worried about it being annoying for new PRs coming into the branch.
A new PR to gauss2 with a bigger diff: https://github.com/thefundamentaltheor3m/Sphere-Packing-Lean/pull/358

My opinion is that @Aayush Rajasekaran and/or @Auguste Poiroux and/or I should assume ownership of the gauss2 branch, and we should not feel the need for one of the Sphere Packing maintainers to approve every single one of these updates to it. The line count moving in the correct direction (while maintaining a clean build) is a pretty strong signal, and we can get full review on each chunk when it eventually gets PR'ed to main.
Agreed, I think it makes sense that merges into gauss2 don't need the approval of a maintainer, whereas merges into main (including ones which started off as lemmas on gauss2) do.
It's already the case that by the perms on github, a maintainer doesn't need to approve a merge into gauss2, correct?
I believe that's true, but have not seen concrete evidence.

Bhavik Mehta said:

It's already the case that by the perms on github, a maintainer doesn't need to approve a merge into gauss2, correct?

Yes, that's correct.
Happy Friday! I'm gonna squash the commits in gauss2, and rebase onto latest main, unless anyone has any objections!
Done! We're now rebased onto main, and back to one commit. Thanks all!
Does CI run on PRs to gauss2? Should we make at least lake build run on those PRs?
I second this, I think we should make lake build run. Maybe we can also consider requiring at least one collaborator approval (not necessarily codeowner approval) for PRs into gauss2.

Actually this should be easy to fix, we just add gauss2 to this list https://github.com/thefundamentaltheor3m/Sphere-Packing-Lean/blob/9170dec227a7a15769c603f85d6e9db50ebdda3e/.github/workflows/build.yml#L7

That will require an intervention for open PRs against the gauss2 branch (specifically 370, 371, 373, and 375). These should all be pretty easy to do, I'm happy to help do it if necessary.
